findings.title: Java MessageFormat syntax introduced into an i18next bundle
findings.body: This bundle is used by the React account console through i18next. Every other entry here uses `{{0}}` interpolation. The new value uses Java MessageFormat placeholders (`{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}`) plus a `{2,choice,...}` pattern, and i18next does not interpret either. Users will see the literal text `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` instead of the attribute name, the numbers and the pluralised word. The previous `{{0}}`-based value should be kept, or pluralisation should be done with i18next.

findings.title: Java choice format used in admin-ui i18next messages
findings.body: This is the admin console (React/i18next) bundle, which interpolates `{{n}}`. The `error-invalid-multivalued-size` value was changed from `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` to `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` with a `{2,choice,...}` construct. i18next renders all of it literally, so the validation error shown in the admin UI is no longer interpolated.

findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian bundle was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, apparently copied from messages_it. Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence. The same mistake appears for `loginTotpStep1` in themes/.../login/messages/messages_lt.properties. Both need a proper Lithuanian translation, or the key should be removed so it falls back to English.

findings.title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
findings.body: `loginTotpStep1` is now the Italian `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` in the Lithuanian login bundle. Lithuanian users will see this sentence on the OTP setup page.

findings.title: Traditional Chinese text in the Simplified Chinese bundle
findings.body: The new `totpStep1` value `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional characters and Taiwanese wording (手機, 應用程式) in the zh_CN bundle. The rest of the file is Simplified Chinese. It should be something like `在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：`.

findings.title: Diff-trimming logic can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
findings.body: The prefix length `start` and suffix length `end` are computed independently, so they can overlap. Example: value="aa", sanitized="a" gives start=1 and end=1. Then `sanitized.substring(1, 0)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Instead of reporting an 'Illegal HTML' message, the verifier crashes the build for exactly the inputs it is meant to report, such as a removed duplicated character or tag. The suffix scan should be bounded so that `end <= min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

findings.title: Missing English counterpart crashes the verifier with RuntimeException
findings.body: The English file path is derived by regex substitution (`resources-community` -> `resources`, `_xx.properties` -> `_en.properties`). If that file does not exist, for example a properties file with no locale suffix or a theme whose English bundle lives elsewhere, a raw RuntimeException is thrown. Because it is not a MojoExecutionException and is not reported as a message, the whole build aborts with an unhelpful stack trace. The missing file should be reported gracefully, or the file should be compared with an empty bundle.

findings.title: Anchor mismatch message omits key and file
findings.body: `Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string` does not include the key or the file name. Every other message from this verifier does. When the build fails on this check across dozens of property files, the offending entry is hard to find.

findings.title: ANCHOR_PATTERN also matches tags that start with 'a'
findings.body: `</?a[^>]*>` matches `<abbr>`, `<address>`, `<area>`, `<audio>` and similar tags, not just `<a ...>`. Such tags are then treated as anchors and must match the English source exactly, which gives confusing 'anchor tag' errors. The pattern should require a word boundary after `a`, e.g. `</?a(\s[^>]*)?>`.
